chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ibn Ribat and Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Safwan all together from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The emancipation of the intoxicated person is not valid.

key_terms.عِتْقُ: Emancipation or manumission of a slave

ai.seo_question: Is the emancipation of a slave by an intoxicated person valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that the manumission (ittq) of a slave by an intoxicated person is legally void, as intoxication impairs the necessary mental capacity (ahl al-ta'abbud) for valid legal transactions. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that the state of inebriation nullifies the validity of unilateral legal acts, distinguishing it from the rulings for the insane or coerced individuals discussed in the same chapter.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Ibn Rabat and Al Husayn Bin Hashim, and Safwan altogether, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘An emancipation by the intoxicated is not allowed’.
